title: Whose Earth
tagline: A concordance of the physical constants both repos use — μ, Earth radius, g0, Earth rotation, reboost energy — with file:line for each and the size of every disagreement at the K2 interface.
pitch: When Aster's arrival v∞ meets Skyhook's release C3, whose Earth is it? This CLI prints a table: constant · Aster value and file:line · Skyhook value and file:line · relative difference · effect on the interface quantities. Measured today: μ 398,600.4418 km³/s² (src/v2/porkchop/delta-v.ts:3) vs 3.986e14 m³/s² (params/rev_a.json orbital.mu_earth_m3s2), 1.1e-6 apart; Earth radius equatorial 6378.137 implied by Aster's parking radius 6,578.137 (delta-v.ts:4) vs mean 6371.0, a literal in physics/skyhook_physics.py:40 and tools/twin/physics.js:21 that rev_a.json never states yet depends on (r_tip 7301 = 6371 + 610 + 320) — recomputing the tether C3 with 6378.137 moves it by ≈0.11 km²/s², 1.3% of −8.06; Earth rotation 0.465 km/s, a literal at skyhook_physics.py:109 not in rev_a.json; g0 9.80665 in both; and reboost energy per kg, where finance/skyhook_finance.py:215 uses 2·v_orb·v_tip = 37.8 MJ/kg while docs/research/mp001_market_pricing.md:37 states 44.8 MJ/kg = 12.4 kWh/kg — a disagreement the study reproduces and reports (the idea tests whether adding the 290→930 km potential-energy term and the ground-relative catch speed reproduces 44.8; [Likely], left to the maintainer). It then recomputes every [Certain] derived number in rev_a.json from its own inputs under each constant set and shows the deltas.
whyNow: Aster INVARIANTS.md INV-021 (frame and quantity established at the consuming boundary), INV-025/026 (numbers trace to a committed constant); Skyhook CLAUDE.md rules 2 and 5 (never hardcode a physics parameter; no magic numbers) against the literals at physics/skyhook_physics.py:40 and :109; K2 (IDEA_KERNELS §1 row 16) needs one Earth; BRIEFING §4.
computes: Recomputation from rev_a.json inputs: v_orb = sqrt(μ/r_com); tier release speed, C3 and apogee at r_tip; tip acceleration; rotation period; V_c = sqrt(2σ/ρ); EQ-6 mass ratios for the five canon cells; the same under Aster's μ and radius; 2·v_orb·v_tip and ½(v_release² − v_catch²) + μ(1/r_low − 1/r_tip) as candidate reboost accountings; a grep-derived file:line table.
dataNeeded: Snapshots of /home/user/skyhook/params/rev_a.json (~6 KB) and /home/user/asteroid-mining-planner/src/v2/porkchop/delta-v.ts (~2 KB) with sidecars; the file:line table saved as example.txt with commits. Under 30 KB.
existingOverlap: Skyhook tests/test_rev_a_physics.py checks the physics module against rev_a.json (internal consistency); Aster src/v2/core/constants/README.md documents its own constants. No cross-repo concordance exists, and the two Skyhook reboost figures have not been reconciled anywhere.
honestyRisks: Declaring one value 'right' — mean and equatorial radius are both legitimate conventions; the study only says the interface must choose and record one. The 44.8 vs 37.8 MJ/kg item is reported as 'does not agree; candidate explanation [Likely]', not as an error. All effects are two-body arithmetic at idea-bank fidelity.
testPlan: whose-earth.test.mjs: recomputation reproduces rev_a.json's v_orb 7.55, C3 −8.06 / −1.94 / +13.05, apogee 85,222 / 397,819 km, 1.99 g, 13.4 min, V_c 2.73, mass ratios 40.32 / 64.30 / 121.83 / 295.27 / 3085.95 to each field's printed rounding; the C3 shift under R = 6378.137 is between 0.10 and 0.12 km²/s² for every tier; 2·v_orb·v_tip = 37.8 ± 0.1 MJ/kg and the alternative accounting is reported with its value; every file:line in the table exists with the quoted token when the checkouts are present (skipped and disclosed otherwise).
landing: Skyhook: a VM-003 entry in docs/verification_memo.md and two new rev_a.json keys (R_earth_km, v_earth_rot_kms) so physics/skyhook_physics.py:40 and :109 import instead of hardcode; a note reconciling finance/skyhook_finance.py:215 with MP-001 §3a. Aster: a constants note for the Momentum lens stating which Earth the interface uses.
notes: Verified R_EARTH_KM = 6371.0 (physics.py:40) and 0.465 (:109) are literals rev_a.json never states, against CLAUDE.md rules 2 and 5; recomputed the 37.8 vs 44.8 MJ/kg disagreement. Small and the interface needs one Earth.

Verified skyhook_physics.py:40 R_EARTH_KM 6371 and :109 0.465 are literals not in rev_a.json (Rule 2 violation), and finance:215 37.8 MJ/kg vs MP-001:37 44.8 MJ/kg; reports conventions, declares nothing right.

The constants table is accurate (delta-v.ts:3-4 μ 398600.4418 and r 6578.137; skyhook_physics.py:40 R 6371 and :109 0.465 literals; finance:215 vs MP-001 44.8). But the '≈0.11 km²/s² shift' only holds if v_orb is held at 7.55 while r_tip moves; recomputing v_orb from μ/R gives 0.029, so the test's 0.10-0.12 band would fail under full recomputation — a convention ambiguity the study should state, not assert.
